risk_register.description: If Email Service (A3) lacks documented API, SLA, or requires custom build, then scheduled report delivery feature (UC5) cannot meet 90% on-time delivery success metric and Phase 2 scope expands by 1–2 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Email Service API documentation unavailable or SLA not confirmed before Sprint 1 build starts
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm Email Service provider (SendGrid, AWS SES, or internal SMTP) and validate API documentation + SLA in week 1 discovery; document rate limits and delivery guarantees
risk_register.contingency: If Email Service is unavailable, pivot to alternative provider (SendGrid free tier confirmed sufficient for 40 scheduled reports/day) or defer scheduled delivery to Phase 3

risk_register.description: If PagerDuty integration scope includes custom escalation policy, on-call scheduling, or incident lifecycle management beyond webhook ingestion, then Phase 2 scope expands by 1–2 weeks and alert response time metric (< 1 hour) may become unachievable.
risk_register.trigger: PagerDuty integration requirements clarified in Sprint 0 and scope exceeds webhook-based alert delivery
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm PagerDuty integration scope is webhook-only in week 1 discovery; validate PagerDuty API documentation and test webhook delivery in sandbox environment
risk_register.contingency: If PagerDuty scope is broader, descope custom escalation policy to Phase 3 and deliver webhook-only alerts in Phase 2

risk_register.description: If PostgreSQL database performance cannot support 15-minute refresh cadence due to data volume or query complexity, then real-time KPI widget feature (UC2) fails and team must architect data warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery) or streaming pipeline (Kafka, Fivetran), adding 3–4 weeks to Phase 2 and $10K–$20K to budget.
risk_register.trigger: Database performance testing in Sprint 0 shows query latency > 2 minutes or data volume > 100M rows prevents 15-minute refresh
risk_register.mitigation: Run database performance baseline in week 1; validate 15-minute refresh is achievable with polling or scheduled queries on current PostgreSQL schema; document query execution plans
risk_register.contingency: If PostgreSQL cannot support 15-minute refresh, pivot to data warehouse (BigQuery) or implement materialized views with incremental refresh strategy

risk_register.description: If Product Owner is not formally assigned or available for backlog prioritization and scope trade-offs during Phase 2–3 sprints, then sprint cycles will stall on scope decisions and timeline will slip.
risk_register.trigger: Product Owner not named in project plan or unavailable for sprint planning ceremonies (> 1 day/week)
risk_register.mitigation: Assign dedicated Product Owner (80% allocation minimum) before Sprint 1 kickoff; establish sprint planning cadence (weekly backlog refinement, bi-weekly sprint planning)
risk_register.contingency: If PO is unavailable, escalate to project sponsor for interim decision-making authority; defer scope trade-offs to steering committee

risk_register.description: If Backend Developer or Product Manager is pulled off critical path due to competing priorities or shared allocation, then critical path tasks (T1, T3, T5, T8, T11, T14, T17, T20, T23) will slip and project deadline (2025-04-10) will be missed.
risk_register.trigger: Backend Developer or PM allocated to competing project or reduced below 80% allocation during Phase 2–3
risk_register.mitigation: Secure written commitment from resource manager that Backend Developer and PM are 80% dedicated to this project through 2025-04-10; document in project charter
risk_register.contingency: If resource is pulled, escalate to steering committee for re-prioritization; identify backup Backend Developer from bench or contractor pool

risk_register.description: If SSO Provider integration (A5) requires custom configuration or has undocumented API, then authentication feature (UC1) will be delayed and all downstream use cases (UC2–UC8) will be blocked.
risk_register.trigger: SSO Provider API documentation unavailable or custom configuration required beyond standard OIDC/SAML setup
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm SSO Provider is existing integration with documented API in week 1; validate OIDC/SAML configuration is already in place and requires no custom build
risk_register.contingency: If SSO requires custom build, defer to Phase 1 extension or use temporary local authentication for Phase 2 development

risk_register.description: If custom report generation (UC3) cannot be completed in < 5 minutes due to query complexity or data volume, then success metric is unachievable and CSM adoption will be low.
risk_register.trigger: Performance testing in Sprint 0 shows report generation latency > 5 minutes for typical CSM query
risk_register.mitigation: Establish performance baseline in week 1; implement query optimization (indexing, caching) and set < 5 minute SLA in Sprint 1 definition of done
risk_register.contingency: If < 5 minute target is unachievable, negotiate extended SLA (< 10 minutes) with CSM stakeholders or implement async report generation with email delivery

risk_register.description: If stakeholder expectations for real-time data refresh diverge from 15-minute cadence assumption, then scope will expand and timeline will slip.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder feedback in Sprint 1 or 2 requests sub-5-minute refresh or continuous streaming
risk_register.mitigation: Validate 15-minute refresh cadence with CSM and Sales leadership in week 1 discovery; document in requirements and get written sign-off
risk_register.contingency: If stakeholders require faster refresh, descope other features or extend timeline; escalate to steering committee for trade-off decision

risk_register.description: If Frontend Developer (60% allocation) is insufficient to deliver UI for all use cases (UC1–UC8) in parallel with backend development, then UI delivery will slip and integration testing will be delayed.
risk_register.trigger: Frontend Developer reports > 80% utilization or UI tasks accumulate > 2 sprints of backlog
risk_register.mitigation: Prioritize UI tasks by use case criticality (UC2, UC3, UC5, UC6 first); use component library and design system to accelerate UI development
risk_register.contingency: If Frontend Developer is overallocated, hire contract UI developer or defer non-critical UI polish (UC4 export formatting) to Phase 3

risk_register.description: If data retention policy (2 years) is not enforced in code or database, then compliance audit will fail and system may violate data governance requirements.
risk_register.trigger: Data retention enforcement not implemented in Sprint 1 or compliance review identifies missing controls
risk_register.mitigation: Implement automated data retention policy (delete records > 2 years old) in Sprint 1; document in architecture decision record and validate in compliance review
risk_register.contingency: If retention policy is not enforced, implement manual data cleanup process or extend retention period pending compliance approval

risk_register.description: If critical path tasks (T1, T3, T5, T8, T11, T14, T17, T20, T23) slip by > 3 days each, then project deadline (2025-04-10) will be missed.
risk_register.trigger: Any critical path task completes > 3 days late or dependency on external system (Email Service, PagerDuty, SSO) is not resolved by planned date
risk_register.mitigation: Establish weekly critical path review in sprint ceremonies; identify blockers early and escalate to steering committee; maintain 5-day schedule buffer
risk_register.contingency: If critical path slips > 3 days, descope Phase 2 features (UC5, UC6) to Phase 3 and deliver Phase 1 + UC2, UC3, UC4 by deadline
